Novokine Combinatorial Receptor Screen
 Ranking and Evaluation Framework
 Jacob Edelson · University of Washington
 April 2026
This document describes the complete ranking and evaluation framework for the Novokine heterodimer screen. It
covers: the experimental scoring system (EXP score); the computational model (v4.0); the scale collision problem
and its resolution; the unified ranking methodology; construct evaluation; and the biological interpretation framework
for prioritizing pairs.

1. Screen Overview and Scope
The Novokine screen evaluates combinatorial receptor pairs for their ability to drive transdifferentiation of primary
human dermal fibroblasts toward a myogenic phenotype. Each construct is a heterodimeric fusion of two receptor
ectodomains expressed from a single lentiviral vector.

2. EXP Score — Experimental Evaluation Framework
The EXP score is the primary evaluation metric for tested pairs. It integrates four phenotypic assays into a single
composite score.

2.2 Normalization Formula
Each assay is independently normalized before weighting:
assay_score = (fold_change - 1.0).clip(min=0) / max_shift_per_assay
EXP = 0.30 x Primary + 0.15 x Respiration + 0.40 x Secondary + 0.15 x Myotube


 clip(min=0): Below-baseline performance is treated as zero, not penalized. A pair that suppresses desmin does
 not receive a negative score.
 max_shift normalization: Each assay is divided by the maximum observed fold-change across all 64 tested pairs,
 yielding a [0, 1] scale per assay.
 EXP range: [0, ~0.55]. The theoretical maximum is 1.0 but is not reached because no single pair saturates all four
 assays simultaneously.

Case
Handling

Use v4.2 composite score as proxy; flagged in "Proxy Used" column

Version note: v4.3 EXP scores supersede v4.2 for all pairs with complete multi-assay data. v4.2 scores are retained as a
reference in the Rank Change column.
3. v4.0 Computational Model
The v4.0 model generates predicted scores for all 1,711 heterodimer pairs, including the 64 tested pairs. It was built
prior to experimental data collection and uses gene-level features to predict pair performance.
3.1 Model Score Formula (Untested Pairs)
v4.3 score = 0.90 x v4.0_model_score + 0.10 x Novelty_score
 v4.0 model score: Gene-level feature composite (GO annotations, GTEx expression, STRING interaction scores,
 receptor family membership).
 Novelty score: Penalizes well-studied pairs; rewards understudied combinations with high potential. Range [0, 1].
 
 v4.3 score range for untested pairs: 0.428 – 0.870.
 
3.2 Model Accuracy Against Experimental Data
Critical finding: The v4.0 model has no demonstrated predictive power for experimental outcome. This was established by
testing model scores against EXP scores for all 64 tested pairs.

Why the model fails: The v4.0 model scores genes independently and combines them additively. It does not encode
receptor complex formation requirements — specifically, it cannot predict whether two receptors will form a functional


signaling complex in fibroblasts. BMPR2+ERBB2 was predicted as model rank #16 (score 0.839) but scored
EXP=0.215 experimentally, because BMPR2 requires a type I BMP receptor partner, not an RTK.
Implication for untested pair rankings: The relative ordering of untested pairs by v4.0 score should be treated as a
hypothesis-generating prior, not a prediction of experimental outcome. Experimental validation is required.

4.1 Tier Boundary Rationale
 0.40 threshold (Strong): Corresponds to pairs with consistent activity across at least 2 assays and a primary
 desmin fold-change > 1.5x. Empirically separates the top cluster from the rest of the distribution.
 0.25 threshold (Moderate): Pairs with reproducible but weaker signal. Often single-assay dominant (high
 secondary, low primary).
 0.10 threshold (Weak): Marginal activity that may reflect noise or context-specific effects. Not prioritized for
 immediate follow-up.
5. The Scale Collision Problem
The original "All Pairs Ranked" sheet in novokine_v43.xlsx contained a structural artifact that invalidated the ranking.
Understanding this problem is essential for correctly interpreting any ranking that mixes tested and untested pairs.
5.1 The Problem
Score Type

The collision: The model score minimum (0.428) exceeds the EXP score for 60 of 64 tested pairs. When both score types are
placed in a single ranking column, all 1,647 untested pairs structurally outrank all 64 tested pairs. This is a unit mismatch — not


a biological finding.

The #1 experimental hit (EGFR+IL6ST) ranked #1,643 in the old all-pairs list. The scale collision affected every tested
pair equally — it is not specific to weak hits. The fix is described in Section 6.
6. Unified Ranking — Recalibration Methodology
The unified ranking resolves the scale collision by placing all 1,711 pairs on a common score scale while preserving
the integrity of experimental data.
6.1 Method: Percentile-Based Rescaling
Two principles guide the recalibration:
 Tested pairs use EXP score directly. Experimental data is ground truth and must not be transformed.
 
 Untested pairs are rescaled via percentile mapping. Each untested pair's v4.0 score is mapped to the EXP
 score range [0, 0.548] based on its percentile rank among all v4.0 scores.
Rescaling formula for untested pairs:
calibrated_score = EXP_min + percentile(v4.0_i, all_v4.0_scores) x (EXP_max - EXP_min)
Where EXP_min = 0.000, EXP_max = 0.548 (EGFR+IL6ST).
6.2 Why Not Regression?
Regression-based recalibration (fitting EXP ~ v4.0) was tested and rejected:
 Pearson r = -0.12 (no correlation). A regression line through uncorrelated data produces calibrated scores that are
 essentially random.
 LOO R2 = -0.041 (worse than the mean). The regression model has negative out-of-sample predictive power.
 
 Percentile rescaling makes no claim about model accuracy — it only maps the model's relative ordering to the EXP
 scale. This is the honest choice.

8. Homodimer Exclusion Criteria
Homodimers (same gene paired with itself) are excluded from the heterodimer ranking system. This is not a data gap
— it is a principled exclusion.
8.1 Why Homodimers Cannot Be Ranked
Criterion
Explanation
Model undefined
The v4.0 model encodes cross-family receptor complementarity. A homodimer has zero cross-family
signal — the model score is not meaningful.
No EXP ground truth
The experimental screen used heterodimeric constructs only. No EXP scores exist for homodimers.
Biological prediction
BMPR2+BMPR2 likely sequesters type I BMP receptors (BMPR1A/BMPR1B), acting as a dominant
negative. ACVR2B+ACVR2B blocks canonical type I receptor pairing. Both are predicted to suppress,
not activate, signaling.
8.2 How to Handle Homodimer Constructs
 Option A (recommended): Exclude from ranking entirely. Report as negative controls if experimental data exists.
 
 Option B (approximate): Floor at the weakest heterodimer containing that gene. For BMPR2: floor =
 BMPR2+FGFR1 (EXP=0.000, rank #1,711). For ACVR2B: no experimental floor exists (all ACVR2B pairs are
untested).
If homodimer constructs were run in the screen, extract their raw assay data and report separately as controls — do not include
in the ranked list.
9. Biological Interpretation Framework
The following principles guide biological interpretation of ranking results. These are not post-hoc rationalizations —
they are mechanistic predictions that can be tested experimentally.
9.1 Why EGFR is the Dominant Hub

(highest of any gene).

9.2 The ACVRL1 (ALK1) Failure Pattern
All 8 tested ACVRL1-containing pairs score below EXP=0.38. 5 of 8 score below 0.20. This is a consistent biological
pattern with a mechanistic explanation:
 Wrong ligand environment: ALK1 has high affinity for BMP9 and BMP10, which are not present in standard
 fibroblast culture medium. A receptor without its cognate ligand cannot signal.
 Endothelial-specific expression: ACVRL1 is normally expressed in endothelial cells, not fibroblasts. The
 downstream signaling machinery may not be present.
 Competitive inhibition: ALK1 competes with ALK2/ALK3 for BMPR2 binding, potentially disrupting endogenous
 BMP signaling rather than augmenting it.
Experimental test: Supplement culture medium with BMP9 (10 ng/mL) and re-test ACVRL1-containing pairs. If the ligand
hypothesis is correct, activity should increase substantially.
9.3 The BMPR2+EGFR Paradox
EGFR is the top hub gene. BMPR2 is in the top 4 strong hits (with NTRK1). Yet BMPR2+EGFR scores EXP=0.115
(No Effect tier, rank #1,332).
 Structural incompatibility: BMPR2 requires a type I BMP receptor partner (BMPR1A, BMPR1B, or ACVR1) to
 form a functional heterotetrameric signaling complex. EGFR is a type III RTK and cannot fulfill this structural role.
 Downstream competition: EGFR and BMPR2 may compete for SMAD adaptor proteins, creating mutual
 inhibition rather than synergy.
 Contrast with BMPR2+NTRK1 (#3, EXP=0.484): NTRK1 provides a complementary neurotrophin signaling axis
 (TrkA-PI3K-AKT) that does not compete with BMP pathway components. This is why BMPR2 works with NTRK1
but not EGFR.
9.4 Model Failure: BMPR2+ERBB2
Model predicted rank #16 (score 0.839). Experimental result: EXP=0.215, rank #19 of 64 (weak hit). The model
overestimated because:
 Both BMPR2 and ERBB2 individually have strong GO annotations and high GTEx expression.
 
 The model scores gene pairs additively — it cannot detect that BMPR2 needs a type I receptor partner, not an
 ERBB family member.
 This failure generalizes: any pair where one receptor has a strict structural requirement for its partner type will be
 overestimated by the v4.0 model.

11.3 Model Retraining
With 64 EXP data points now available, the v4.0 model should be retrained using EXP scores as the target variable.
Current model r = -0.12 means the untested pair rankings are essentially random. A retrained model could
substantially improve prioritization of the remaining 1,647 untested pairs.


 Minimum viable dataset: 64 pairs is sufficient for a regularized model (LASSO or ridge regression) with
 cross-validation.
 Key features to add: Receptor complex formation compatibility (type I/II pairing rules), ligand availability in
 fibroblast culture, endogenous expression level in primary fibroblasts (not GTEx bulk).
 Expected improvement: Even modest r = 0.4 would make the untested pair ranking substantially more useful
 than the current r = -0.12.
